channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: 'Nina Roza' director: 'I was inspired by a real case of a child painter prodigy'
item.description: The director of a film nominated by Canada for next year's Oscars has told FRANCE 24 she was inspired by stories of a child painter prodigy, as well as the idea of identity and what you leave behind when you change countries. The film "Nina Roza" tells the story of a Bulgarian man who leaves his homeland with his daughter and sets himself up as an art curator in Canada.

item.title: UK’s Burnham on a mission to build public support EU reset
item.description: While he insists it would be unthinkable to rejoin the bloc without another referendum, British PM Andy Burnham has nevertheless reopened the debate over Brexit. After striking a deal that brings the UK and the EU closer on issues including food export control standards, youth mobility and carbon emissions, he's set to discuss the future of the relationship with Brussels in the coming weeks and will present the results of the talks in December. It comes despite criticism from a host of former Conservative prime ministers.

item.title: The French mayors refusing to back presidential candidates
item.description: Tuesday marks the opening in Paris of the 108th Congress of French Mayors, where the presidential race is a contentious issue. Candidates need 500 mayor endorsements to run, yet nearly half of mayors this year say they refuse to endorse anyone. France 2 and Caitlin Brown have more.

item.title: France's femicide orphans: The invisible victims of violence against women
item.description: In France, 111 women were killed by their current or ex-partners in 2025 alone, leaving behind dozens of children. How can they rebuild their lives without their mother? How can they seek help? In this episode of France in Focus, we meet Cloé and Eva-Louise, whose world collapsed when their father brutally murdered their mother. FRANCE 24's Natacha Vesnitch, Olivia Bizot, Clément Di Roma and Aurore Cloé Dupuis report.

item.title: WATCH: Detroit Lions help feed their community this Thanksgiving
item.description: ABC News' Will Reeve shares how the Detroit Lions are carrying on a Thanksgiving tradition of giving back to those in need.

item.title: Russian drone flies into Poland during overnight strikes on Ukraine, Warsaw says
item.description: A Russian drone violated Polish airspace late on Monday night during Moscow's latest wave of long-range strikes on Ukraine, the Polish military said.

item.title: Who really owns the land in Albania that Jared Kushner wants to develop?
item.description: Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama has vowed that Kushner's resort project will go ahead as planned. But an ongoing investigation by Albania's state prosecutor into forged land titles could halt the project.

item.title: Millwall FC face partial stadium closure over 'ableist and homophobic' chanting
item.description: Millwall have been punished with a partial stadium closure after two FA crowd rule breaches for ableist and homophobic chanting.

item.title: Senegal regain AFCON title after successful appeal at sport arbitration court
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport on Tuesday ruled in favour of Senegal in the appeal to reclaim the Africa Cup of Nations title, 10 months after a chaotic final against Morocco. Senegal won the match in January but was stripped of the title in March, when it was awarded to Morocco.

item.title: Rwanda's malaria cases on the rise: Climate change leads to more mosquitoes
item.description: In Rwanda, malaria cases are on the rise due to climate change. Higher temperatures and prolonged rainfall are creating more breeding grounds for mosquitoes. According to researchers, the risk of infection could increase by as much as 20 percent by 2100 in the Rift Valley. Our correspondent Aurore Bayoud reports on Rwanda's efforts to tackle the problem.

item.title: 'Political hunting ground': French presidential candidates campaign mayors' congress
item.description: Candidates in next year’s French presidential election descended on the 108th Congress of French Mayors in Paris on Tuesday, hoping to win endorsements for their campaigns. France 24’s Luke Shrago reports.

item.title: Trump's role in Huang's Nvidia return under scrutiny
item.description: Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia was greeted with triumph by US President Donald Trump, and the AI chipmaker's stock price was sent soaring. But the national security implications of Huang's extra-marital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, as well as Trump's intervention in the operations of a company in which he holds stock, have stirred anger in Congress, with members from both parties vowing to investigate.

item.title: WATCH: Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys celebrate 30 years of giving back
item.description: ABC News' Rhiannon Ally highlights how the Dallas Cowboys are celebrating three decades of giving back to their community during Thanksgiving.

item.title: In South Africa, parents' homemade sensory room helps children with ADHD
item.description: Determined to help their children, parents in a South African township have transformed a discarded shipping container into an underwater-themed sensory room using recycled plastic bottles, cut-out flowers and ferns. Originally designed for children with conditions including ADHD and epilepsy, the space is now benefiting the wider community.

item.title: DR Congo and Kenya agree to restore ties
item.description: After years of strained relations over the conflict in eastern Congo, Kinshasa and Nairobi are moving towards a diplomatic reset. DR Congo's President Felix Tshisekedi met his Kenyan counterpart William Ruto over the weekend and they agreed to to restore normal ties and deepen economic and regional cooperation. Emmet Livingstone reports.

item.title: Powerful storm threatens East Coast as Thanksgiving approaches: Forecast and track
item.description: A developing storm is expected to bring heavy rain, powerful winds and coastal flooding to parts of the East Coast on Wednesday and Thanksgiving Day.

item.title: Trump administration assured Nvidia Huang wasn't facing criminal charges, sources say
item.description: Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia's CEO on Monday.

item.title: Israeli strikes on Gaza kill senior Hamas security official and six other people, medics say
item.description: Israeli air strikes on the devastated Gaza Strip killed Brigadier General Naeem Abu Nahel, director-general of the Palestinian territory's Internal Security Service on Tuesday, the ministry said. Another six people, including two police officers and a 17-year-old teenager, were killed in Israeli strikes across the enclave.

item.title: Advances in health and medicine: From space, ‘you discover things that are hidden' back on Earth
item.description: When kids look up at the night sky and marvel at the moon and the stars, the mysteries of space can spark a sense of wonder and curiosity. One of France's most beloved astronauts, Thomas Pesquet, joins Eve Irvine to take us one step beyond with his new book, "Space in 100 Questions", offering space enthusiasts of all ages an otherworldly glimpse into the Final Frontier!

item.title: WATCH: Amazon drone crash raises safety concerns
item.description: The FAA Is investigating after an Amazon delivery drone crashed onto a garage near Detroit after dropping off a package.

item.title: NHS England chief executive to step down in spring
item.description: The head of NHS England is stepping down ahead of the body's abolition next year.

item.title: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO in sudden reversal after Trump intervention
item.description: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday under pressure from US President Donald Trump, drawing approval/plaudits/cheers from Wall Street and criticism from US lawmakers. The sudden reversal was the latest twist in the fallout from Huang’s admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

item.title: FA chair had to sign NDA to view FIFA documents on World Cup sell-off
item.description: Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has now viewed some FIFA documents on the World Cup sell-off but had to sign a nondisclosure agreement, Sky News has learned.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir shares how NFL teams are giving back this Thanksgiving
item.description: As millions prepare for a day of thanks this holiday season, NFL teams across America are serving meals to their communities this Thanksgiving.

item.title: Baby P's mother loses latest bid for prison release
item.description: Baby P's mother has lost her latest bid to be released from prison - but the Parole Board has recommended she is moved to an open jail.

item.title: Macron mulls enshrining fiscal rules in French constitution
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has suggested reviving a 15-year-old proposal to enshrine a framework for public finances in the constitution, as a possible response to concerns in financial markets over France's fiscal trajectory. "If there is still volatility by January, thinking about a 'golden rule' of the type proposed in 2011 could be an idea worth exploring," Macron said, speaking to Le Figaro.

item.title: French chefs battle it out at Paris egg mayo championships
item.description: It is one of the most common starters in the French culinary repertoire, but the humble egg mayonnaise is also a test of any chef's prowess. The World Egg Mayonnaise Championship this week brought together cooks from across France and beyond to find out who makes the best.

item.title: Simple Minds at 50: Still alive and kicking
item.description: From Glasgow teenagers to global rock stars, Simple Minds have spent nearly five decades filling stadiums and creating some of the defining songs of their generation. Now, as the band celebrate 50 years with new music "Sacrosanct" and a major 2027 tour, Jim Kerr tells Eve Jackson about the music, the memories and the moments that shaped Simple Minds, including the night he discovered they were number one in America by telegram in a hotel in Nice.

item.title: What should it cost to insure a home in wildfire country?
item.description: Some California homeowners have spent thousands making their homes safer from wildfires. Yet all that work has barely made a dent in their insurance bills. Should they be getting a bigger break?

item.title: 'Nothing will ever be the same' for Jensen Huang and Nvidia after his return
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Tuesday, November 24: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia dominates the papers. In other news, leaked records shed new light on Russian military losses in Ukraine. Also, the UK will host the 2035 Women's World Cup. Finally, a devilled eggs world championship crowns its winner.

item.title: AFCON: Ten months on, court to rule on 2025 winner
item.description: Ten months after the Africa Cup of Nations final was chaotically played on the field between Morocco and Senegal, the title will be awarded Tuesday by sports’ highest court. The Court of Arbitration for Sport set the target Monday to publish the verdict of its panel of three judges on Senegal’s appeal to regain the title the team won on the field in Morocco in January and then lost in a legal case in March.

item.title: Two men arrested over suspected burglary at William and Kate's home
item.description: Two men have been arrested over a suspected burglary at William and Kate's Norfolk home.

item.title: Inmate who murdered Ian Huntley given second whole-life prison sentence
item.description: An inmate who murdered Soham killer Ian Huntley has been sentenced to a second whole-life prison term.

item.title: WATCH: Preparing for annual White House turkey pardon
item.description: Two turkeys named Freedom and Feather are set to get Thanksgiving pardons from President Donald Trump Tuesday.

item.title: ICE raids add to jitters ahead of Thanksgiving travel rush
item.description: Travellers in the US are heading into a particularly stressful holiday travel period this week. Recent network outages for US airlines and the Federal Aviation Administration have raised concerns about flight delays and cancellations ahead of Thanksgiving on Thursday. This, plus ICE agents ramping up arrests at airports, has made many travellers anxious.

item.title: Rep. Jimmy Gomez to resign after House Ethics report he engaged in sexual misconduct
item.description: Gomez lost his reelection bid in November.

item.title: Thousands evacuated from UK concert after release of 'unknown substance'
item.description: British police said they evacuated 12,000 people from ​a concert venue in Manchester, northern England, after the release of an "unknown substance" required some in the crowd to be treated and one person to be taken to hospital. Police ​declared ‌a major incident late on Sunday after staff at the ⁠Co-op Live arena alerted them at 10 p.m. (2200 GMT) that people in the crowd had fallen ill during ‌a performance by US rapper Don Toliver.

item.title: Spain set to head to polls in snap election that could boost far right
item.description: Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez seeks to thwart grim polls as polarised Spain holds an election on Sunday that could propel the opposition conservative Popular Party (PP) and the far right to power. The outcome will be closely watched across Europe as it opens a cycle of elections over the next 12 months that could reshape the balance of power within the European Union.

item.title: Is Russia preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite?
item.description: German media reports, citing unnamed German military and BND spy agency sources, have claimed that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite in the coming weeks, giving it the capability to destroy other satellites. In response, NATO chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space. France 24’s correspondent in Berlin Nick Holdsworth has the details.

item.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
item.description: Doctors are fighting an uphill battle against disinformation about routine vitamin K shots given to newborns in the hospital. It helps prevent a rare but devastating bleeding disorder.

item.title: They attended Trump's meme coin dinner. It didn't go well
item.description: Trump's meme coin dinners have sparked intense controversy. These two guests attended his latest on Sunday — and agreed to provide NPR inside access.

item.title: Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one
item.description: Threatt Filling Station in Luther, Okla., was the first Black-owned gas station on Route 66. At a time when Black families needed the Green Book to find places to stay, eat, use the bathroom, it provided fuel and respite.

item.title: For workplace culture champions, Jensen Huang's return is 'unfathomable'
item.description: Some who have worked to promote diversity and inclusion in Silicon Valley say Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO sends a message that all that matters is money.

item.title: Bleeding, birth defects: Congo residents sue over alleged mining pollution
item.description: A landmark lawsuit in Congo sees 27 residents accuse a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine of poisoning their community and the government of failing to protect them.

item.title: Meet Colombia's fuzzy 'water guardians'
item.description: High in the Colombian Andes, a growing number of volunteers are racing to save an unusual plant that helps supply water to millions — one tiny seedling at a time.

item.title: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
item.description: Investigators say companies with ties to Donald Trump Jr's investment firm, 1789 Capital, have profited since his father's reelection.

item.title: Heat deaths up 76% on previous record as total reaches new high in England
item.description: Heat deaths reached a record high this year in England, new data shows.

item.title: 'This is a developing incident': Tests to identify unknown substance ongoing after concert evacuation
item.description: Tests are ongoing to identify an unknown substance that led to a mass evacuation from Manchester's Co-op Live arena during a Don Toliver performance.

item.title: Outgoing Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch pushes back on Trump attacks
item.description: As Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch prepares to retire, the historian defended the institution and pushed back against attacks leveled by the Trump administration.

item.title: US military to detonate toxic explosives despite lead dust fears
item.description: The US Army will proceed with plans to detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa after a federal appeals court gave the controversial proposal the go-ahead.

item.title: Senegal restored as Africa Cup of Nations champions
item.description: Senegal has been awarded the Africa Cup of Nations title after successfully appealing against the decision to strip them of it.

item.title: WATCH: Storms on both coasts threaten Thanksgiving week travel, Macy's parade
item.description: The storm set to slam New York City could ground Macy's parade balloons for the first time in 55 years.

item.title: Gisele Pelicot 'deeply shocked' as nude photos of her sent to media
item.description: Gisele Pelicot has said she is "deeply shocked" and "humiliated" after nude images of her were sent to the media without her consent to promote a new book about coercive control.

item.title: Trump says he 'convinced' Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang
item.description: Jensen Huang has been reinstated as president and CEO of Nvidia.

item.title: Sky News documentary wins International Emmy
item.description: Sky News has won an International Emmy for 24 Hours In The Kill Zone.

item.title: What led to Democrats' sweeping victories in Georgia: ABC News analysis
item.description: ABC News analyzes factors of why Democrats performed well in Georgia on Election Night.

item.title: WATCH: Celebrating Tom Jackson's extraordinary life and legacy
item.description: The ESPN legend and former All-Pro linebacker died at 75.

item.title: WATCH: How AI tools can help lock in the lowest prices for holiday shopping
item.description: More than 40% of consumers have used AI assistants for online shopping, according to Adobe, and ABC News’ Becky Worley tried them to see how they can help with your shopping.

item.title: Dems holding 12 debates in 2028 cycle, requiring candidates denounce 'dark money'
item.description: The Democratic National Committee announced on Monday that it will hold 12 primary debates in the 2028 presidential primary cycle.

item.title: Deadly fire at confectionery factory kills 24 as rescuers search for dozens still missing
item.description: A deadly fire that tore through a confectionery factory in Indonesia has claimed the lives of 24 people, with 34 others still missing.

item.title: Democrat Chuck Hubbard wins recount, flips North Carolina US House seat
item.description: Democratic Chuck Hubbard will win the election in North Carolina's 5th congressional district, the Associated Press projects.

item.title: Rahm Emanuel: Schumer should commit to stepping down as leader after next Congress
item.description: Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel, a potential 2028 presidential candidate, joined "This Week" to discuss what Democrats should do after their historic midterm victory.

item.title: DNI Clayton: Putin is 'not America's friend in Ukraine'
item.description: The director of national intelligence appeared on ABC's "This Week" Sunday.

item.title: Man who was lured to remote villa and held for 15 hours rescued after being tied up and beaten
item.description: A man has been rescued after he was lured to an isolated villa, held for 15 hours, tied to a chair, beaten, and threatened with death, police in Spain say.

item.title: Meet the Ukrainian energy workers dodging drones to bring people's electricity back
item.description: "The first thing the guys and I do is look at where we can hide."

item.title: At least 11 dead after suspected cartel leader 'El Chapo Isidro' captured in Mexico
item.description: An outburst of violence has killed at least 11 people after Mexican authorities captured suspected cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro.

item.title: WATCH: Tips for hosting Friendsgiving this year
item.description: Digital creator Kerra Masella shares her tips for planning and hosting a Friendsgiving celebration, from getting organized ahead of time to making friends feel welcome around the table.

item.title: WATCH: Is travel insurance worth it after the FAA ground stop?
item.description: Katy Nastro, travel correspondent at Flighty, shares what travelers can do to protect themselves.

item.title: WATCH: New health warning on doomscrolling: What to know and tips to break the habit
item.description: A Lancet Psychiatry report calls problematic internet use a global health concern, affecting more than 1 in 10 people. ABC News’ Dr. Jennifer Miao explains the impact and how to protect yourself.

item.title: WATCH: Reporter goes undercover as porch pirate
item.description: A New York Times reporter went undercover as a porch pirate to help identify the best ways to keep your home and packages safe as package deliveries ramp up this holiday season.

item.title: Nidal Hasan is set to be executed. The military's other death row cases are in limbo
item.description: There are three other former soldiers who are on the military’s death row.
